items.b: DOYLE NEW YORK TAKES $457,700 FOR 12.46 CARATS, AND 1890 SAPPHIRES BEAT THEIR BOOK BY 180%
items.t: The top lot, a D colour VS2 emerald cut, cleared its $350,000 high estimate by 30.8%. A pair of antique earrings holding a 4-carat Ceylon and a 4.17-carat Kashmir sapphire made $140,200 against $30,000 to $50,000, which is 2.80 times the high. Four of the top five beat the book; the sale made more than $8 million.

items.b: A ROYAL BROOCH LED THE ELMWOOD'S COVERAGE AND FINISHED FOURTH OF FOUR ON PRICE
items.t: The Verdura unicorn brooch from Queen Elizabeth II's lady-in-waiting made 23,750 pounds, or $32,400, at the 19 August London sale. A 1927 Van Cleef and Arpels feather brooch made 75,000 pounds, 3.16 times as much. Every dollar conversion in the report reconciles to one rate near $1.363 to the pound.

items.b: KAGEM SHOWS ROUGH EMERALDS IN JAIPUR FOR NINETEEN DAYS, AND PUBLISHES NO PRICE
items.t: The 13th India Rough Gemstones Sourcing Show opened 24 August and runs to 11 September, with more than 60 Indian manufacturers on the council's own count. Kagem's May book in London took $26.8 million at $146.08 a carat. No value, carat weight or lot count has been published for Jaipur.

items.b: FOSSIL'S SALES FELL 4.9% AND THE WATCH LINE FELL 1.5%
items.t: The quarter to 4 July puts net sales at $209.7 million against $220.4 million. Traditional watches went from $178.4m to $175.7m. Leathers fell 31.1% and jewellery 11.2%, and leathers alone are about half the whole decline. Across six months traditional watch sales rose 0.4%.

items.b: A ROUGH STONE PASSED VISUAL SCREENING AS NATURAL AND FAILED ONLY AT INFRARED
items.t: The Israeli Diamond Institute reports a stone submitted 18 August that looked like ordinary natural rough, drew a preliminary and self-qualified flag from a CVD screening device, and was classified Type IIa by FTIR. Single-source, the testing laboratory itself, and no carat weight published.

items.b: GOLD WRITTEN BACK AT $4,622.30, DOWN $21.60 ACROSS TWO SESSIONS
items.t: Kitco and TradingEconomics sat $1.54 apart, or 0.033%. Silver written back at $68.55 on a 0.19% gap, up 0.99% on yesterday, narrowing the ratio to 67.43 from 68.27. Platinum and palladium held a sixth session at $1,881.00 and $1,336.00, their two sources 0.83% and 1.40% apart.
